plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of blush-white blossoms cover bare branches before the leaves appear. Petals drift down like snow in spring breezes, and crowds gather beneath the trees for hanami picnics.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April, with peak bloom often falling in early April in central Japan and in Washington, D.C.
plants.location: Japan (Tokyo and Kyoto) and Washington, D.C., USA
plants.funFact: Nearly all Yoshino cherry trees are clones, grafted from a single original tree. That is why a whole city's trees can burst into bloom within days of each other.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding golden trumpets surrounded by pale, swept-back petals brighten woodlands and meadows. Drifts of them carpet the ground, bringing cheerful color after the grey of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April, with flowers still widespread in early April
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the woodlands and meadows of England, Wales, and France
plants.funFact: The wild daffodil is the inspiration for countless garden varieties. All parts of the plant contain toxic alkaloids, so deer and rabbits leave it alone.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Satin-smooth, cup-shaped blooms stand tall on sturdy stems in rows of vivid color. In the Dutch bulb fields, whole fields of red, yellow, and pink stripe the landscape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early April to early May, with the first fields opening in early April in the Netherlands
plants.location: The Netherlands (Lisse and the Bollenstreek bulb region)
plants.funFact: Tulips came from the mountains of Central Asia. In the 1630s, their bulbs were so prized in Holland that single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house.
